kill_argument: The title asks whether default tabular classifiers are calibrated and whether isotonic recalibration helps; the pre-specified tests answer neither. H1 is relative and is measured by an estimator whose noise floor (0.01-0.04) is two to eight times the 0.005 margin, with the two arms scored on different numbers of bins. By the paper's own account, its 'contradicted' means that default LR is miscalibrated on two datasets where a linear model fits poorly (phoneme AUC 0.81). That is the textbook caveat to the textbook result. H2a and H2b both turn on electricity, whose random splits straddle neighbouring half-hours and whose one leakage check measured drift instead. Everything else is descriptive. The body says this plainly, but the abstract still offers the debiased ECE's same-sign agreement as reassurance, and the related work presents the crew's own tabulation of a third party's archive as that paper's finding. What I attacked that held: all 197 macros map to the right run metric; all 25 per-dataset categories recompute; the 48 plain table numbers match describe; plan.json has changed only in tasks and gates since results.

findings.text: The abstract presents the debiased ECE as corroboration: 'a debiased estimator, reported descriptively, points the same way on every dataset'. The body says the opposite about what that agreement is worth. The estimator keeps about 0.6 of any floor difference with its sign, so its agreement 'is not confirmation' (Sec. 3.4, Sec. 4.1, Table 3 caption). It also moves adult from inconclusive to holds. This was conceded at code-r1 F2: the replication licence was dropped because ece_db agreement is close to vacuous. A reader of the abstract alone takes the sentence as a robustness check. Remedy (cheap): delete the clause, or add 'which, since it keeps most of any floor difference, is not independent confirmation'.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex lines 52-54 (abstract) vs lines 289-293, 440-443, 621-623; plan.json disclosures[2]; reviews/code-r1 F2

findings.text: Related work attributes to Manokhin and Gronhaug (2026) per-dataset counts that the cited paper does not report: 'isotonic lowered the mean log-loss of random forests on 18 of 30 datasets but that of HistGradientBoostingClassifier on only 4 of 30'. sources/notes.md says Appendix A 'gives no per-dataset breakdown'. The counts are the Scout's own summary of the authors' released archive, made by a scratchpad script that was not kept and is not a logged run (sources.json manokhin2026 note). They are also selective. The same tabulation gives Brier counts, and Brier is this paper's own H2 metric: isotonic was better for RF on 13 of 30 and for HGB on 14 of 30. On Brier, the RF/HGB contrast the sentence draws disappears. Claim c-manokhin-archive carries the same attribution. Remedy (cheapest): drop the sentence and keep the Appendix A ranks. Otherwise, label it as the crew's tabulation of the released results, back it with a logged data-prep run that hashes the archive, and report Brier beside log-loss.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex lines 156-159; claims.jsonl c-manokhin-archive; sources/notes.md manokhin2026 Archive table and Appendix A paragraph; sources/sources.json manokhin2026.note

findings.text: The AI-use statement misreports the code review. It says 'The code review passed with no critical finding before any analysis run', and lists code round 1 among stages whose 'last round ... passed with minor findings still open'. In fact code-r1's verdict was revise, with two major findings open (F1 one-hot width assertion; F2 ece_db replication licence) and one minor. There was no code round 2. main started at 07:43:43Z, under two minutes after code-r1 (created 07:42:00Z) and 33 s after the re-run of unit-tests finished. The Reviewer first checked the fixes at results-r1 (08:11Z), after all five analysis runs. Sec. 3.6 likewise says only that 'the Reviewer checked the code against the approved method'. The plan's bar (no open critical finding before analysis; analysis_plan[3]) was met, so this is a disclosure error, not a protocol breach. But the AI-use statement is the record of oversight and must be exact. Remedy: state the verdict (revise; 2 major, 1 minor), that F1 was fixed and F2/F3 narrowed before main without a second code review, and that results-r1 verified them.
findings.evidence: paper/ai-use.tex lines 20-28; paper/main.tex lines 353-356; reviews/code-r1/review.json; reviews/results-r1/review.json; runs/main/run.json started; log.jsonl lines 50-54

findings.text: Sec. 6 opens with 'Every amendment below is recorded in plan.json (disclosures) and in the crew's log, with the plan's hash'. plan.json disclosures has three entries, which cover items 1-3. Item 4 (the code fix) is logged (07:43:18Z) but is not a disclosure. Items 5 and 6 are decisions made after results: sensitivity (c) failed its stated purpose; the sens-ncal overall was dropped; the machine-epsilon log-loss was not reported; Platt was omitted from the reliability diagrams. They appear in neither the disclosures nor any log line. The current plan.json (sha256 855bfa1d) is also not logged, though it differs from the logged c3ebd78c only in tasks and gates. Remedy: add disclosures for items 4-6 with a log line and hash, or reword the lead sentence to say which items are recorded where.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex lines 715-716, 745-759; plan.json disclosures (3 entries); log.jsonl

findings.text: The planned machine-epsilon log-loss sensitivity was computed but suppressed. It is planned in threats[8] 'so readers can see how much of any difference the epsilon makes', and in analysis_plan[6] (logloss_mach). Yet the paper asserts twice that RF's log-loss 'depends on the clipping constant', and the dropped sensitivity is the evidence for that claim. Remedy (cheap; describe metrics already hold *_logloss_mach_mean/sd): add the values to Table 4 or quote them for uncalibrated RF.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex lines 492-493, 705-707, 756-757; plan.json design.threats[8], analysis_plan[6]; runs/describe/metrics.json *_logloss_mach_*

findings.text: The abstract's H1 sentence ('is contradicted: RF scored lower, with RF-minus-LR differences of ... on bank-marketing and ... on phoneme') omits that H1 held on electricity (0.0270 [0.0232, 0.0308]) and was inconclusive on adult. Read alone, 'RF scored lower' sounds general. Remedy: 'RF scored lower on two of four datasets; the published direction held on electricity'.

'Platt scaling, fitted on the logit, changed little' (Sec. 4.4) and 'Platt scaling on the logit changed little throughout' (Sec. 5) contradict the paper's own numbers. For RF on electricity, Platt minus none was -0.0029 [-0.0032, -0.0027]. That is the same size as isotonic's -0.0028, which the paper treats as the one H2a 'holds' beyond the margin. For HGB on electricity it was -0.0008 [-0.0010, -0.0006]. Remedy: 'changed little except for the tree models on electricity'.

The AI-use statement still has placeholders that are now stale. 'this item is to be updated after it' refers to the paper review. 'no replication.json exists' is no longer true: replication.json (passed: true, created 2026-11-19T12:52:00Z) is now in the workspace. Both items must be filled in before the submission gate.

brier1950 is cited beyond what was read. It is a DOI-only entry, and sources.json says 'Cite only as the origin of the Brier score'. The paper cites it, with gneiting2007, for the property that strictly proper scores 'reward honest probability forecasts' (claim c-proper-scores). This also makes the AI-use sentence 'each is cited for no more than was read' inaccurate. Remedy: cite gneiting2007 alone for propriety, and brier1950 only where the score is defined.
findings.evidence: paper/main.tex lines 176-177; paper/ai-use.tex lines 38-41; sources/sources.json brier1950.note; claims.jsonl c-proper-scores

findings.text: The introduction says that Platt or isotonic 'can repair miscalibration once the calibration set has about 1,000 cases or more' (Niculescu-Mizil and Caruana 2005). The source puts the 200-1,000 threshold on isotonic matching or beating Platt; Platt works with fewer cases (claim c-nm-isotonic-data; notes Sec. 5, Fig. 7). Related work states it correctly. Remedy: reword the introduction to match.

Some result numbers are typed rather than macros, and one caption does not match its figure. 'against 15 for LR' (line 431) and 'against 15' (line 551) are LR ece_bins results; macros exist (\AdultLrNoneEceBins, \ElecLrNoneEceBins, ...). 'smaller in size than $0.00005$' (line 470) is a typed bound on a result. Fig. 1's caption says the dagger is on electricity's label, but the figure prints it on the category labels ('holds†', 'no difference†').

The title promises more than the tests deliver. 'Are Default Tabular Classifiers Calibrated, and Does Isotonic Recalibration Help?' invites absolute answers. The confirmatory test of calibration is relative (RF vs LR) and estimator-bound. The isotonic tests end inconclusive and no difference, with both verdicts resting on electricity. Remedy: a title that names what was tested, e.g. 'Random Forest versus Logistic Regression Calibration and Isotonic Recalibration under scikit-learn Defaults: Pre-Specified Tests on Four OpenML Datasets'.
